````text
1	# 用 FM-1 控制 agent
2	
3	FM-1 和 agent 可以往兩個方向接：
4	
5	1. **FM-1 控制 coding agent**：琴鍵、LED、螢幕變成 Claude Code、Codex 等 CLI agent 的實體控制台。
6	2. **agent 操作 FM-1 做音樂**：agent 透過 MIDI / SysEx 寫入音色、pattern、編曲。
7	
8	## FM-1 Agent Deck
9	
10	[FM-1 Agent Deck](https://github.com/kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck)（kevinelliott，GPL-3.0）是一套獨立韌體，把 FM-1 變成 coding agent 的桌上控制台。以下都來自它的 README `[上游]`。
11	
12	**它是取代合成器的韌體，不是 SLOOP 上的 plugin。** 刷著 Agent Deck 時 FM-1 不發聲；刷回原廠或其他韌體才回到樂器。它不讀其他韌體的 projects，其他韌體的資料能不能撐過一趟 Agent Deck 沒有測過，所以先備份。
13	
14	### 硬體怎麼對應
15	
16	| FM-1 | Agent Deck |
17	|---|---|
18	| 27 個琴鍵 | 每鍵一個 agent slot（2 頁共 54 個），按下選取 |
19	| 琴鍵 LED | 狀態：off EMPTY、dim IDLE、solid WORKING、2 Hz 閃 BLOCKED（等你處理）、快閃 ERROR |
20	| 240×240 螢幕 | GRID（列表或方塊）、DETAIL（OUTPUT / INFO / DIFF）、APPROVALS、MENU、ABOUT |
21	| `REC` / `SAVE` | approve / approve 並不再詢問 |
22	| `FX` / `ENV` | deny（Esc）/ interrupt（Ctrl-C） |
23	| `PLAY` | continue；在空 slot 上開新 agent |
24	| `PRESETS` + `SEQ` | 選一個 prompt preset 送出；對 BLOCKED agent 會排入佇列 |
25	| `ARP` | 這個 agent 的 auto-approve 開關 |
26	| `K4` | 跳到下一個需要你處理的 agent |
27	| `GLO` 按住 + `REC` / `FX` … | 一次套用到所有適用的 agent |
28	
29	裝置上不能打字：自由輸入的 prompt 還是要在 terminal 裡打，裝置只送 preset。
30	
31	### 架構
32	
33	```text
34	FM-1 (Agent Deck firmware)
35	   ⇅  USB-MIDI channel 16
36	host/agtdeck.py  (電腦上的 Python daemon)
37	   ⇅  Herdr socket API (newline JSON)   或   tmux CLI
38	Herdr  /  tmux  →  Claude Code、Codex、opencode ...
39	```
40	
41	daemon 每秒輪詢 backend，只把變動送給 FM-1；FM-1 每秒回 heartbeat，螢幕 header 顯示 `HOST OK` 或 `NO HOST`。只支援 USB-MIDI，沒有 Bluetooth。
42	
43	**Herdr 是比較好的 backend。** Herdr 原生回報每個 pane 的 agent 狀態（Idle / Working / Blocked / Done），tmux backend 則是看指令與畫面文字的 heuristic，會誤判。README 記錄 2026-11-08 對 Herdr 0.9.5 實測過 discovery、狀態、approve、deny、interrupt、prompt 與 `agent.start`；其他 Herdr 版本可能改了 socket method 名稱。我平常就用 Herdr，所以 Herdr 整合是這個專案對我最有意思的部分。
44	
45	### 不刷機就能試
46	
47	模擬模式（不需要 FM-1），指令照 README：
48	
49	```sh
50	git clone https://github.com/kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck.git
51	cd fm-1-agent-deck
52	
53	python3 host/agtdeck.py --backend auto --simulate
54	sh host/test_simulate.sh        # 開三個用完即丟的 tmux session 自我測試
55	```
56	
57	只看 Herdr backend：`python3 host/agtdeck.py --backend herdr --simulate`（要有正在跑的 Herdr）。出問題時 `python3 host/agtdeck.py --doctor` 會逐項檢查。
58	
59	真的刷了 Agent Deck 並接上 USB 之後的硬體模式：
60	
61	```sh
62	pip install mido python-rtmidi
63	python3 host/agtdeck.py --backend auto
64	```
65	
66	線上播放器：[在瀏覽器裡跑 Agent Deck](https://kevinelliott.github.io/fm-1-agent-deck/play/?fw=agtdeck&script=demo.txt)，是 fm1-emu 跑真正的韌體 package，按 **Start** 播一段腳本化的 session。
67	
68	!!! note "0.7 改名"
69	    0.7 把專案的檔案與指令從 `agentdeck` 改成 `agtdeck`：package `agtdeck-0.7.fwsc`、daemon `host/agtdeck.py`、設定在 `~/.config/agtdeck`。網路上舊文章裡的 `agentdeck.py` 已經不存在。
70	
71	### 狀態與風險
72	
73	README 的 Status（2026-11）寫得很誠實：作者的 FM-1 實機跑的是 **0.6.2**，用 daemon 接真的 Herdr session；最新的 **0.7** 只差版本字串與 daemon 檔名，在 GitHub 上 build 並簽章，**只在 emulator 跑過，還沒上實機**。prompt queue、pipelines、auto-approve 規則多半是對 stub backend 測的，預期會有粗糙處。版本見[資源地圖](../resources.md)。
74	
75	README 說它的 base（Dinghy 0.5）在程式碼裡同時接受舊 Puya（`0x856014`）和新 UCUN（`0xB36014`）的 JEDEC ID。但我**沒有找到在新款 UC25HQ80 晶片上實機跑 Agent Deck 的明確回報** `[調研]`。我的晶片見[我的機器](../device-log.md)，晶片差異見 [Flash 晶片](../hardware/flash-chips.md)。
76	
77	!!! warning "auto-approve 保持關閉"
78	    `ARP` 開啟後 daemon 會自動 approve 這個 agent 的 prompt。它有 `auto_never` 清單（`rm -r`、`git push`、`sudo` 等），但 README 自己說這只是文字 pattern match，不是 sandbox，換個寫法的危險指令照樣通過。auto-approve 預設關閉、daemon 重啟後也會忘掉；我會一直讓它關著，避免誤觸按鍵就讓 agent 改檔案或執行指令。
79	
80	## 不刷 Agent Deck 的替代方案
81	
82	| 方案 | 怎麼做 | 取捨 |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| [Trireme](https://github.com/ignis32/trireme_fm1) | Vial 相容的 USB HID 鍵盤 / macro pad，按鍵送快捷鍵 | 不需要 host daemon；但沒有 agent 狀態回饋。作者標明是 vibe-coded、沒逐一手測 `[上游]` |
85	| [CTL-1](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-ctl) + Python `mido` | FM-1 送 MIDI，自己寫 script 轉成任意 agent API 呼叫 | 最彈性，CTL-1 還有自己的 GM 音色；狀態回顯要自己做 `[調研]` |
86	| 保留音樂韌體，用它的 MIDI 輸出 | SLOOP 等韌體照常發聲，host daemon 接它的 MIDI | 不必換韌體；能拿到哪些按鍵、旋鈕、螢幕回饋，取決於該韌體的 MIDI protocol `[調研]` |
87	
88	## agent 操作 FM-1 做音樂
89	
90	SLOOP 的 [web editor](../firmware/sloop/web-editor.md) 透過 USB MIDI 和機器即時同步，protocol 記在 SLOOP repo 的 `web/EDITOR_PROTOCOL.md` `[上游]`。這是讓 agent 寫入音色與 pattern 最直接的介面，但目前沒有針對 2.8.x 的現成 agent 工具。
91	
92	社群有兩個 editor skill，都是 MIT、中文 README `[上游]`：
93	
94	| Skill | 目標韌體 | 平台 | 格式 |
95	|---|---|---|---|
96	| [fm1-sloop-editor-2026](https://github.com/hunterxiong2026/fm1-sloop-editor-2026) | SLOOP **2.4.1** | Windows（`ctypes` + `winmm.dll` 直送 SysEx） | DeepSeek Harness skill（`~/.dsh/skills/`） |
97	| [fm1-felucca-editor-2026](https://github.com/hunterxiong2026/fm1-felucca-editor-2026) | Felucca **v1.5** | 只支援 Windows | Claude skill（`SKILL.md`） |
98	
99	兩者都綁定舊版韌體的 SysEx 參數表，也不能在 macOS 上直接跑。適合當「agent 透過 MIDI 控制 FM-1」的參考實作，**不要拿來對 SLOOP 2.8.x 或 SLOOP 3 寫入 project**。
100	
101	## 不刷機的試用清單
102	
103	- [ ] 在[線上播放器](https://kevinelliott.github.io/fm-1-agent-deck/play/?fw=agtdeck&script=demo.txt)看完 demo，翻一遍 GRID、DETAIL、APPROVALS
104	- [ ] clone repo，跑 `--simulate` 對自己的 Herdr session
105	- [ ] 跑 `sh host/test_simulate.sh`，看 tmux heuristic 的結果
106	- [ ] 用 `--doctor` 確認 Herdr socket 找得到
107	- [ ] 在本機 [fm1-emu](emulator.md) 開 `agtdeck-0.7.fwsc`
108	- [ ] 讀完 README 的 Arrival day 與 Risk notes，再決定要不要刷；刷之前照[注意事項](../getting-started/cautions.md)與 `AGENTS.md` 的 preflight
109
````

1	# 自製韌體環境
2	
3	目標是把 **改 code → host simulator → fm1-emu → 批准 → 實機** 整條鏈跑通，再談功能。基礎是 [fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base)（MPL-2.0，beta）：它在 felucca-bsp 之上提供螢幕、按鍵、LED、音訊、MIDI、storage，以及跑同一份 app 的 host simulator。
4	
5	**狀態（2026-11-17）：host simulator、實機套件 build、fm1-emu 兩種晶片開機都已跑通；還沒刷進實機。**
6	
7	## 結構
8	
9	```text
10	third_party/fm1-base/      git submodule（它自己再帶 felucca-bsp 於 bsp/）
11	firmware/hello/            fm1-base template 的原樣複本，用來驗證整條鏈
12	firmware/<app>/            之後的 app
13	tools/jieli/               JieLi toolchain（gitignore）
14	tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK/    JieLi AC79 SDK，固定 tag（gitignore）
15	```
16	
17	這符合上游的建議：把 `template/` 複製到自己的 repo，fm1-base 放在旁邊當 submodule。`tools/build.py APP_DIR` 接受任意位置的 app 目錄。
18	
19	## 指令
20	
21	| 指令 | 作用 | 我跑過嗎 |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `just fw-setup` | 初始化 submodule、安裝 Python 工具（`fw` dependency group） | 是 |
24	| `just fw-test [app]` | build host simulator 並跑 `tests/basic.txt`，產出截圖與 WAV 到 `firmware/<app>/build/host/` | 是，全部 `ok` |
25	| `just fw-toolchain` | 下載 JieLi toolchain 與 AC79 SDK 到 `tools/`（約 1.2 GB） | 是 |
26	| `just fw-build [app]` | build 實機套件 `firmware/<app>/build/*.fwsc` | 是，約 17 秒，產出 `template.fwsc`（616 KB，identity `FM-1_1100`） |
27	
28	## 前置需求（macOS）
29	
30	- `uv`、`just`、Xcode command line tools（`cc`）。
31	- **`brew install libraqm`。** fm1-base 的字型產生器（`tools/gen_font.py`）用到 OpenType features，需要 Pillow 帶 libraqm。macOS 的 Pillow wheel 編譯時沒有包含它（`HAVE_RAQM = False`），所以 `pyproject.toml` 設了 `no-binary-package = ["pillow"]`，讓 Pillow 從原始碼對 Homebrew 的 libraqm 編譯。沒裝的話 `gen_font.py` 會報 `not supported without libraqm`。`[實機]` host 端
32	- 實機 build 另外需要 **Docker**：JieLi toolchain 只有 Linux x86-64，`build.py` 在 macOS 上會自動把每個工具放進 `linux/amd64` 容器執行。
33	
34	## 兩段式 build
35	
36	| | Host simulator | 實機套件 |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| 指令 | `build.py APP --host` | `build.py APP` |
39	| 需要 | 本機 C 編譯器 | JieLi toolchain + AC79 SDK + Docker |
40	| 產出 | `build/host/<name>_host` | `build/<name>.fwsc` |
41	| 用途 | 日常迭代、邏輯與畫面測試 | 模擬器與實機 |
42	
43	Host simulator 讀一份腳本（`tests/basic.txt`）注入按鍵與 MIDI、檢查狀態、存截圖與音訊。這是讓 agent 自己驗證改動的主要手段，不需要任何硬體。
44	
45	## Build 結果
46	
47	`just fw-build hello` 的輸出（2026-11-17）：app 226,264 B；RAM code 9,296 / 32,768 B；`.data+.bss` 76,452 / 98,304 B；build 自帶的檢查全部 `ok`（沒有 soft-double、register 存取只在 felucca-bsp 內）。
48	
49	在 fm1-emu 開機 `[模擬]`：
50	
51	| 晶片 | 結果 |
52	|---|---|
53	| `uc25hq80` | 開機到 TEMPLATE 畫面，5 秒內 12 次 flash erase / program |
54	| `p25q80` | 同上，12 次 |
55	
56	兩種晶片行為一致。這只是開機與寫入次數，「改設定 → 重開 → 讀回」還沒做。
57	
58	!!! note "之前卡住的地方"
59	    第一次 build 失敗是因為 Docker daemon 的 proxy 連不上，拉不到 `debian:bookworm-slim`（`build: cannot start the toolchain container`）。修好 Docker 的網路後就正常。遇到同樣訊息先查 `docker pull --platform linux/amd64 debian:bookworm-slim` 能不能成功。
60	
61	## 預設的 template 帶 Bluetooth
62	
63	`firmware/hello/fm1.toml` 是 `ble = true`，會用到 SDK 裡 JieLi 的 Bluetooth library（binary only）。如果第一次 build 想降低變數，可以加 `--no-ble`（產出 `NAME-usb.fwsc`）。
64	
65	## Release 與另開 repo 的問題
66	
67	fm1-base template 附的 release workflow（透過共用的 [zvenson/fm1-build](https://github.com/zvenson/fm1-build) 產生 build attestation，Firmware Hub 才會標 built from source）假設的是**獨立的 firmware repo**：app 在 `app/`、fm1-base 在 `base/`、根目錄有 `./build.sh`。放在這個筆記 repo 的子目錄不符合那個配置，所以我把複本裡的 `.github/` 拿掉了。
68	
69	結論：在本機迭代、刷自己的機器，子目錄就夠。**等某個 app 要正式 release 時，再把它搬到獨立 repo，並以 submodule 引回這裡。**
70	
71	## 自製韌體的規則
72	
73	寫在 `AGENTS.md`，重點：
74	
75	1. 先 `just fw-test`，再用 `just emu-run` 在**兩種晶片**各跑一次，才提實刷。
76	2. 存檔只走 fm1-base 的 storage 層，它處理新舊晶片的 JEDEC ID。不自己寫 flash 位址。
77	3. 自製韌體每一次實刷都要我批准，和裝別人的韌體一樣。
78	4. build 產物不進 git。
79	
80	## 下一步
81	
82	- [x] 跑通 `just fw-build hello`
83	- [x] `just emu-shot firmware/hello/build/template.fwsc` 兩種晶片都開機
84	- [ ] `just emu-run firmware/hello/build/template.fwsc` 兩種晶片各一次，改設定、重開、確認保存
85	- [ ] 批准後刷進實機，按鍵 → USB MIDI → host 端 `mido` 腳本收得到
86	- [ ] 開第一個自己的 app：最小的 MIDI controller / macro pad（按鍵送 MIDI、螢幕顯示 layer）
87	- [ ] 依 [Agent Deck 試用](../firmware/agent-deck/index.md)的心得，決定 agent 控制台是 fork Agent Deck 還是在 fm1-base 上重寫
88
````
</details></tool-use>

# 我的機器

這台 FM-1 目前的狀態與操作歷史。任何對實機的操作，做之前先讀這頁，做完更新這頁。這頁的內容都是 `[實機]`。

## 現況

| 項目 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 型號 | M-VAVE FM-1 |

## 這代表什麼

- 這台是**新晶片**機。裝任何自訂韌體前都要確認它寫明支援 UC25HQ80，見[兩種 Flash 晶片](hardware/flash-chips.md)。SLOOP 2.8.5 有支援。
- m-bootloader 在這顆晶片上測試很少，暫不安裝。這也表示 SLOOP 3 暫時不刷。
- 出廠是 015，不是 016，所以沒有 016 覆寫 preset 區的問題。不要用 M-UPGRADE 升到 016，除非確定要。

1	# Agent Deck 操作速查
2	
3	整理自上游 README 的 Controls reference，對應韌體 0.7。`[上游]`，除非另外標示。我自己的試用與刷機紀錄在[概觀](index.md)。
4	
5	## 啟動
6	
7	```sh
8	just agtdeck-run        # FM-1 已刷 Agent Deck 並接上 USB；預設用 Herdr backend
9	just agtdeck-doctor     # 連不上時先跑這個：檢查 MIDI 埠、設定、agent CLI、Herdr
10	```
11	
12	螢幕右上角從 `NO HOST` 變成 `HOST` 就是連上了。daemon 停掉或 USB 拔掉會回到 `NO HOST`，重新接上會自動重新同步。
13	
14	macOS 上這台裝置的 MIDI 名稱可能仍顯示成 `Felucca`（系統快取了之前 SLOOP 的名稱，USB 產品名其實是 `FM-1 AGTDECK`）。daemon 認得，不影響使用。`[實機]`
15	
16	## 琴鍵與 LED
17	
18	27 個琴鍵各是目前這一頁的一個 agent slot，按下去就選取那個 agent。LED 表示狀態：
19	
20	| LED | 狀態 | 意思 |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| 不亮 | EMPTY | 這個 slot 沒有 agent |
23	| 微亮 | IDLE | 在等輸入 |
24	| 恆亮 | WORKING | 忙碌中 |
25	| 閃爍 2 Hz | BLOCKED | **需要你**：等批准或有問題要回答 |
26	| 快閃約 6 Hz | ERROR | agent 或 backend 回報錯誤 |
27	| 恆亮 2 秒後轉微亮 | DONE | 剛完成一輪 |
28	| 慢速脈動 1 Hz | UNKNOWN | 有 agent 但狀態無法分類 |
29	
30	功能鍵的燈也會反映選取中的 agent：WORKING 時 `PLAY` 亮，BLOCKED 時 `REC` 閃，開了 auto-approve 時 `ARP` 亮。
31	
32	`OCT-` / `OCT+` 換 slot 頁，兩頁共 54 個 slot。
33	
34	## 最常用的幾個動作
35	
36	| 想做的事 | 按 |
37	|---|---|
38	| 選一個 agent | 它的琴鍵，或轉 **SELECT** |
39	| 跳到下一個需要我的 agent | 轉 **KNOB 4** |
40	| 批准目前的提示 | **`REC`** |
41	| 批准並且不再問 | **`SAVE`** |
42	| 拒絕 | **`FX`**（送 Esc） |
43	| 中斷 | **`ENV`**（送 Ctrl-C） |
44	| 按 Enter | **`SEL`** |
45	| 在 agent 的選單裡移動 | **KNOB 2**（上下）、**KNOB 3**（左右），再按 `SEL` |
46	| 看這個 agent 的輸出 | **`EDIT`**（同時在電腦上聚焦那個 pane）；再按切換 OUTPUT / INFO / DIFF |
47	| 回列表 | **`HOME`**；在列表上再按一次切換「列表 / 方塊」 |
48	| 看所有待批准的 | **`GLO`** |
49	
50	## 全部控制項
51	
52	動作由電腦上的 daemon 對**選取中的** agent 執行。
53	
54	| 控制 | 動作 |
55	|---|---|
56	| 琴鍵 | 選 slot（空的也可以選） |
57	| **SELECT** | 在 agent 之間移動選取 |
58	| **`PLAY`** | 開始 / 繼續；在純 shell 上：在裡面啟動預設 agent；在**空 slot** 上：開一個新 agent |
59	| **`REC`** | 批准 |
60	| **`SAVE`** | 批准且不再問（畫面上有那個選項時） |
61	| **`FX`** | 拒絕（Esc） |
62	| **`ENV`** | 中斷（Ctrl-C） |
63	| **`SEL`** | Enter |
64	| **KNOB 2** / **KNOB 3** | 上下 / 左右方向鍵 |
65	| **`LFO`** | 切換 agent 的 mode（Shift+Tab） |
66	| **PRESETS** | 選一個預設 prompt（顯示在底部那一行） |
67	| **`SEQ`** | 送出選好的預設 prompt。對 BLOCKED 的 agent 會先排隊，等它有空再送 |
68	| **`ARP`** | 切換這個 agent 的 auto-approve。預設關閉，daemon 重啟後不保留 |
69	| **KNOB 1** | 往回捲 DETAIL 的輸出 |
70	| **KNOB 4** | 跳到下一個需要你的 agent（BLOCKED → ERROR → DONE） |
71	| **`EDIT`** | DETAIL 頁 |
72	| **`HOME`** / **`GLO`** | GRID 頁 / APPROVALS 頁 |
73	| **ALGORITHM** | 輪流切換 GRID → DETAIL → APPROVALS → MENU → ABOUT |
74	| **`OCT-` / `OCT+`** | 上 / 下一頁 slot |
75	| **MASTER** | 提示音音量 |
76	
77	## 一次處理多個
78	
79	**按住 `GLO` 再按** `REC` / `FX` / `ENV` / `SEQ` / `ARP`：對所有適用的 agent 做同一件事。批准或拒絕全部 BLOCKED、中斷全部 WORKING、把預設 prompt 送給全部 IDLE / DONE、關掉所有 auto-approve。
80	
81	**按住功能鍵再點琴鍵**（游標不動，按住時相關的鍵會亮起來提示）：
82	
83	| 組合 | 動作 |
84	|---|---|
85	| `REC` + 鍵 | 批准那個 agent |
86	| `FX` + 鍵 | 拒絕那個 agent |
87	| `ENV` + 鍵 | 中斷那個 agent |
88	| `SEL` + 鍵 N | 回答第 N 個選項（輸入數字 1–9） |
89	| `SEQ` + 鍵 N | 把第 N 個預設 prompt 送給選取中的 agent |
90	| `PLAY` + 鍵 | 開始 / 繼續那個 agent；空鍵則在那裡開新 agent |
91	| `SAVE` + 鍵 | 把選取中的 agent 搬到那個鍵（已有則交換） |
92	| `LFO` + 鍵 | 標記 / 取消標記。有標記時，`GLO` + 動作只作用在標記的那幾個 |
93	| `ARP` + 鍵 | 切換那個 agent 的 auto-approve |
94	| `SEQ` 按住約 1 秒 | repeat mode：agent 每完成一輪就再送一次選好的 prompt |
95	
96	`SAVE` + 鍵可以用來整理版面：把真正的 agent 搬到前面，shell 留在後面。slot 配置會存在 `~/.config/agtdeck/slots.json`。
97	
98	## 畫面
99	
100	五個頁面，用 **ALGORITHM** 輪流切換：
101	
102	| 頁面 | 內容 |
103	|---|---|
104	| **GRID** | 所有 agent 的列表或方塊。一列是：狀態色邊條、slot 編號、狀態圖示、名稱、種類（`CL` Claude Code、`CX` Codex、`OC` OpenCode、`SH` shell…）、在該狀態的時間、旗標、context 用量條 |
105	| **DETAIL** | 選取 agent 的輸出、INFO、DIFF |
106	| **APPROVALS** | 等你批准的清單；沒有時顯示 ALL CLEAR |
107	| **MENU** | SELECT 移動、`SEL` 選、`FX` 返回。可開新 agent、送 prompt、看 event log、關 agent、改設定 |
108	| **ABOUT** | 韌體與協定版本、host 是否連線、backend、uptime |
109	
110	顏色就是狀態：琥珀色是在等你，綠色是完成，紅色是壞了，白色是工作中，灰色是閒置。
111	
112	列上的旗標：`A` auto-approve、`R` repeat、`+` 已標記、`Q` 有排隊的 prompt。
113	
114	## Auto-approve
115	
116	預設關閉，建議維持關閉。開了之後 daemon 會自動批准該 agent 的提示，但會先比對 `auto_never` 清單（預設含 `rm -r` / `-f`、`git push`、`git reset --hard`、`sudo`、`--force`、`drop table`、`mkfs` / `dd`），命中就不批准並發出警示。上游自己說明這是文字比對，不是安全保證。
117	
118	## 設定檔
119	
120	`~/.config/agtdeck/config.json`，不存在時用預設值。`python3 vendor/fm-1-agent-deck/host/agtdeck.py --print-config` 會印出完整預設。常改的：
121	
122	| 欄位 | 用途 |
123	|---|---|
124	| `presets` | 預設 prompt 清單（預設 9 個），也可以是多步驟的 pipeline |
125	| `default_agent` | `PLAY` 在空 slot 上啟動哪一種 agent |
126	| `projects` | 開新 agent 時可選的目錄 |
127	| `auto_never` | auto-approve 絕不自動批准的字樣 |
128	| `nag_minutes` | agent 一直 BLOCKED 時每隔幾分鐘再提醒 |
129	| `follow` | 有 agent 被 block 時選取自動跳過去 |
130	
131	## 一定要插 USB：沒有藍牙 `[上游]`
132	
133	FM-1 的晶片有藍牙，但 Agent Deck 用不到。上游寫明 "USB-MIDI only"：它的基底 Dinghy 完全沒有藍牙程式，要支援 BLE MIDI 得從頭寫無線電 driver，不是開個開關。協定本身不挑傳輸方式，所以將來可能加，目前（0.7）不行。
134	
135	## Herdr 裡為什麼會突然出現 `continue` { #continue }
136	
137	`continue` 不是 daemon 自己亂送的，下面幾個動作都會送出它：`[上游]`（對照 `host/agtdeck.py`）
138	
139	| 你做了什麼 | 結果 |
140	|---|---|
141	| 對一個**已經有 agent** 的 slot 按 `PLAY`（或 `PLAY` + 鍵） | `PLAY` 的意思是「開始 / 繼續」：pane 裡已經有 agent 時就送 `continue`；是空的 shell 才啟動新 agent |
142	| 按 `SEQ` | 送出目前選好的 preset。**預設 preset 清單的第一個就是 `continue`**，沒轉過 PRESETS 就是它 |
143	| 對 BLOCKED 的 agent 按 `SEQ` | 不會立刻送，**排隊**（列上出現 `Q`），等 agent 有空才送出。所以會在你按完一段時間之後才冒出來，看起來像自己送的 |
144	| 按住 `SEQ` 約 1 秒 | repeat mode（列上出現 `R`）：agent 每做完一輪就再送一次，最多 `repeat_max`（預設 10）次 |
145	| `GLO` + `SEQ` | 送給所有 IDLE / DONE 的 agent（有標記時只送給標記的） |
146	
147	要避免：
148	
149	- 先看列上有沒有 `Q` 或 `R`。`R` 再按住 `SEQ` 一次就停。`Q` 是排隊中的 prompt，在 MENU → THIS AGENT 的 queued prompts 可以清掉。
150	- 不想要 `continue` 當預設，在設定檔的 `presets` 把它拿掉或換到後面。
151	- 想開新 agent 要對**空的** slot 按 `PLAY`。
152	
153	## 我遇到的
154	
155	- Herdr 裡 shell pane 也會佔 slot，我的 50 個 pane 大半是 shell，真正的 agent 被擠到後面。沒有隱藏 shell 的設定，目前只能用 `SAVE` + 鍵手動整理，或用 **KNOB 4** 直接跳到需要處理的 agent。`[實機]` host 端
156	- 完整說明見上游 [README](https://github.com/kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck#controls-reference) 與[一頁式 cheat sheet](https://kevinelliott.github.io/fm-1-agent-deck/cheatsheet.html)。

19	|---|---|---|
20	| 從網頁上傳 sample 檔案 | SLOOP 的 [Web Editor](../firmware/sloop/web-editor.md)（4 個 slot，可以丟長錄音進去 CHOP）、官方 Workbench、Mini-Grain、ECHOFIELD 的 companion web app | `[上游]` |
21	| 讓 FM-1 當 USB 音效卡的**輸出端**，收主機播的聲音 | CTL-1（iPad 的聲音會從 FM-1 播出來，我實測過）、FM1 Audio Router | `[實機]` CTL-1 |
22	| 收主機的 USB 音訊並錄成 sample | ECHOFIELD 的說明寫 "your own samples (or recorded over USB)"，但沒說是哪個方向 | 沒查證 `[調研]` |
23	
24	所以「手機或網頁 + FM-1」的組合可以做到 sampler 的效果：在手機或電腦上錄好、剪好，再上傳到支援 sample 的韌體。ChoralRoot 做不到，它的聲音全是合成的，沒有 sample 引擎（GRAIN 引擎是對它自己生成的素材做 granular，不能載入外部 sample），USB 音訊也只有輸出到主機的方向。`[上游]` `[實機]`
25	
26	Firmware Hub 上找 sampler 類韌體：在 [catalog](https://thefirmwarehub.com/) 搜尋 sample、granular。
27	
28	## USB-C：device，不是 host
29	
30	FM-1 是 USB device。USB 鍵盤直接插在 FM-1 上不會動，因為兩邊都是 device，中間需要一個 host：電腦、手機或 USB MIDI host box。
31	
32	**例外（更正 2026-11-17）**：ChoralRoot 0.31 起有 **Options → USB Host**，打開後 USB-C 變成 USB MIDI host，可以直接接一台 USB MIDI 鍵盤，或用一條 USB-C 線把兩台 FM-1 互接。限制：FM-1 不供電，鍵盤要透過有供電的 hub 或 OTG 轉接頭；只支援 full-speed；開著時電腦、USB audio、更新都不能用；每次開機都回到一般 device 模式，不會存。`[上游]`（[release notes](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ChoralRootFM1/blob/main/docs/releases/0.31.md)）其他韌體預設仍是 device。
33	
34	反過來，電腦對 FM-1 可以做的事很多：
35	
36	- 接收琴鍵與旋鈕送出的 MIDI note / CC。
37	- 送 MIDI 回去控制合成器或 sequencer。
38	- 用支援 USB audio 的韌體直接數位錄音。
39	- 透過雙向 MIDI / SysEx 自訂螢幕內容、LED 狀態與 host 控制協定（Agent Deck 就是這樣做的）。
40	- 用自訂韌體讓 FM-1 變成 HID 鍵盤 / 滑鼠（Trireme）。
41	
42	注意不同韌體的 MIDI mapping 不同。不能假設每個實體按鍵在原廠韌體下都會送出獨立事件。`[調研]`
43	
44	## TRS MIDI IN
45	
46	需要 **TRS-to-DIN MIDI 轉接線**。沒聲音時試另一種型式（Type A / Type B）。
47	
48	SLOOP 下的 channel 對應：
49	
50	| MIDI channel | 播放 |
51	|---|---|
52	| 1、2、3 | synth track 1、2、3 |
53	| 10 | drum track |
54	| 其他 | 目前選取的 track |
55	
56	可以在 GLO → MIDI 改。MIDI clock in 可從 USB 或 TRS 進來（GLO → SYSTEM → SYNC）。
57	
58	## USB audio（SLOOP）
59	
60	SLOOP 下 FM-1 同時是一個名為 **"Felucca"** 的 USB audio 輸入：44.1 或 48 kHz、16-bit stereo、class compliant，不需要 driver。錄到的是 master 輸出，跟耳機聽到的一樣。MIDI、Web Editor、installer 都走同一條線。
61	
62	- 音量：按住 `HOME` 進選單 → **USB AUDIO**。`MASTER` 跟著 master 旋鈕；`FULL` 是固定滿音量，適合沒有輸入增益的錄音介面。
63	- 安裝後第一次要拔插一次，電腦才會重新辨識成 MIDI + audio 裝置。
64	
65	## 用電腦接收 MIDI 的最小範例
66	
67	確認電腦看到的 MIDI port（需要 `pip install mido python-rtmidi`）：
68	
69	```python
70	import mido
71	
72	print(mido.get_input_names())
73	with mido.open_input(mido.get_input_names()[0]) as port:
74	    for msg in port:
75	        print(msg)
76	```
77	
78	這是通用的 `mido` 用法，不是某個上游專案的指令。port 名稱依韌體而定。
79
````
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Agent Deck wire protocol v6
2	
3	How the FM-1 (running the Agent Deck firmware, a Dinghy fork) and the host
4	daemon (`host/agtdeck.py`) talk. Everything runs over **USB-MIDI, channel 16**
5	(status byte low nibble `0xF`). BLE MIDI is a possible later transport — the
6	protocol is transport-agnostic — but for now it is USB only.
7	
8	**Division of labour.** The device is a dumb panel: it reports every control
9	and renders what it is told. The host owns everything that needs judgement —
10	what a knob does to an agent, which prompt preset is armed, when to chime,
11	how far the detail text is scrolled. Only what must feel instant stays on
12	the device: the selection cursor, the page, the LEDs, the per-slot clocks.
13	
14	v6 (firmware 0.6) is a superset of v5 (0.5), v4 (0.4), v3 (0.3), v2 (0.2)
15	and v1 (0.1); all
16	interoperate — see [Versioning](#versioning).
17	
18	## Why channel messages, not SysEx
19	
20	Dinghy's platform owns SysEx: the firmware updater (OTA) speaks SysEx, and
21	`midi_get()` in `platform.c` never delivers SysEx (or any system message other
22	than clock/transport) to the app. So host→device data **cannot** use SysEx
23	without forking the platform's USB stack and risking the updater. Instead:
24	
25	- Device→host uses plain Note/CC messages (the HYP-1 "remote mode" precedent).
26	- Host→device uses a **framed byte stream packed into CC values**. Every CC
27	  data byte is 7-bit clean (0–127) by definition, and every payload this
28	  protocol carries is either a small integer (< 128) or printable ASCII
29	  (32–126), so no escaping/encoding layer is needed at all.
30	
31	MIDI is slow (USB-MIDI is not the bottleneck here; the FM-1 screen is), so the
32	host sends deltas, keeps frames small (≤ 48 payload bytes), and refreshes the
33	device at most ~2–4 Hz.
34	
35	## Device → host (channel 16)
36	
37	| Message | Encoding | Meaning |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| Note On `0x9F` | note = 48 + key (48–74), vel = 127 | Piano key *k* (0–26) pressed. Also selects slot `page*27 + k` on the device — unless a button is held (v3): then it is a **chord**, the note goes out alone and the cursor stays |
40	| Note Off `0x8F` (or Note On vel 0) | note = 48 + key | Key released |
41	| CC 102–115 | value 127 = down, 0 = up | Buttons. CC = 102 + button id (Dinghy `BTN_*`): 102 OCT−, 103 OCT+, 104 FX, 105 SEL, 106 ENV, 107 LFO, 108 EDIT, 109 GLO, 110 HOME, 111 SAVE, 112 ARP, 113 SEQ, 114 PLAY, 115 REC. Both edges are sent, so the host can treat any button as a held modifier |
42	| CC 85–91 | relative: 65–127 = clockwise (value − 64 detents), 1–63 = counter-clockwise (64 − value detents), 64/0 = no-op | Encoders. 85 SELECT, 86 ALGORITHM, 87 K1, 88 K2, 89 K3, 90 K4, 91 PRESETS. SELECT moves the device's own cursor (reported as CC 120), so 85 is sent only where the host owns it: on the MENU page (v3), and always by v1, where the host ignores it |
43	| CC 121 | value = page (0 GRID, 1 DETAIL, 2 APPROVALS, 3 MENU, 4 ABOUT in v6) | Page changed on the device, or the answer to a HELLO_ACK. *v3* |
44	| CC 7 | absolute 0–127 | MASTER pot (device sends on change ≥ 2). It is the chime volume; the host ignores it |
45	| CC 116 | value = protocol version (v1 sent a constant 1, which is its version) | Heartbeat, every 1000 ms. This is how a daemon started after the device learns what it is talking to |
46	| CC 117 | value = protocol version | Hello, sent once at boot |
47	| CC 120 | value = slot index | Selection changed on the device (key press, SELECT encoder, or page change). v2 also sends it in answer to a HELLO_ACK, so a fresh daemon learns where the cursor is |
48	
49	### What the panel does (implemented by the daemon)
50	
51	| Control | Action on the selected agent |
52	|---|---|
53	| **Keys** | Select that slot (empty slots can be selected too) |
54	| **SELECT** encoder | Move the selection across occupied slots |
55	| **PLAY** | Start / continue. On an **empty slot**: spawn the default agent in a new pane; it lands in that slot |
56	| **REC** | Approve the pending prompt |
57	| **SAVE** | Approve *and don't ask again*: picks the prompt's numbered "Yes, and don't ask again / allow all…" option if one is on screen; otherwise does nothing and says so |
58	| **FX** | Deny (Esc) |
59	| **ENV** | Interrupt (Ctrl-C) |
60	| **SEL** | Enter |
61	| **K2** / **K3** | Up·Down / Left·Right arrow keys — with SEL, enough to answer any menu an agent puts up |
62	| **LFO** | Cycle the agent's mode (Shift+Tab) |
63	| **PRESETS** encoder | Arm a prompt preset (shown on the footer line) |
64	| **SEQ** | Send the armed preset as a prompt |
65	| **ARP** | Toggle auto-approve for this agent: the daemon approves its prompts as they appear. The row shows `A`, the ARP LED lights |
66	| **K1** | Scroll the DETAIL text back through the agent's output (the host re-sends the window) |
67	| **K4** | Jump the selection to the next agent that needs a human (BLOCKED, then ERROR, then DONE) |
68	| **EDIT** | DETAIL page; the daemon also focuses that pane on the computer |
69	| **HOME** / **GLO** / **ALGORITHM** | GRID page / APPROVALS page / cycle pages (device-local) |
70	| **OCT−/OCT+** | Slot page down/up (device-local; the host tracks it) |
71	| **GLO held +** REC / FX / ENV / SEQ / ARP | The same action for every agent it applies to: approve or deny all BLOCKED, interrupt all WORKING, send the preset to all IDLE/DONE, auto-approve off everywhere |
72	| **MASTER** | Chime volume (the platform's master volume) |
73	| **REC / FX / ENV held + key** | Chord (v3): approve / deny / interrupt *that* slot's agent, selection unchanged |
74	| **SEQ held + key N** | Chord (v3): send prompt preset N to the selected agent |
75	| **SEL held + key N** | Chord (v3): type the digit N (1–9) — answer a numbered option |
76	| **PLAY held + key** | Chord (v3): start / continue that slot's agent; on an empty slot, spawn one there |
77	| **SAVE held + key** | Chord (v3): move the selected agent to that slot (swap if taken); the host follows with a SELECT frame |
78	| **LFO held + key** | Chord (v3): mark / unmark that slot's agent. While any are marked, the GLO-held actions apply to the marked agents only; GLO + LFO clears the marks |
79	| **ARP held + key** | Chord (v3): toggle auto-approve on that slot's agent |
80	| **PLAY held + PRESETS** / **SEQ held + PRESETS** / **SEL held + K1** / **LFO held + K4** | An encoder turned while a chord button is held: choose the agent PLAY starts / set the repeat count / scroll DETAIL a page / step through the marked agents. The button then does nothing on release |
81	| **GLO** while already on the APPROVALS page | Select the agent that has waited longest (oldest BLOCKED, else ERROR, else DONE); the host follows with a SELECT frame. (HOME while already on the GRID is the device's own: it flips the GRID between rows and boxes, v6) |
82	| **K1** on the MENU page | Move the menu cursor a page (7 rows) at a time |
83	| **SEQ held ≥ 0.7 s**, no key | Toggle repeat mode: the armed preset is re-sent each time the agent comes to rest |
84	| **EDIT** on the DETAIL page | Cycle DETAIL through the agent's output, the host's INFO summary and its DIFF summary (the frames are the same DETAIL lines) |
85	| **MENU page:** SELECT / SEL / FX | Move the menu cursor / pick / back (the host draws the page with TEXT frames) |
86	
87	A chord button acts on *release* when no key was tapped meanwhile (with a
88	v3 device; on press with older firmware, which cannot chord). While any
89	button is held the device shows the host's KEYLEDS instead of the slot
90	states, so the keys can show what a tap would do.
91	
92	## Host → device (channel 16): the CC frame stream
93	
94	Two CCs carry everything:
95	
96	- **CC 118 — frame control.** Value `0x10 | type` (0x10–0x1F) = *start frame*
97	  of that type (aborts any partial frame). Value `0x20` = *end frame*
98	  (commit). Value `0x7F` = *reset*: clear all slots, names, detail lines.
99	- **CC 119 — data.** Value = one payload byte of the open frame. Payload bytes
100	  are all < 128 by construction (integers are small; text is ASCII 32–126).
101	  Max 48 payload bytes per frame; the receiver drops longer frames.
102	
103	Frame types:
104	
105	| Type | Name | Payload |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| 0x01 | SLOT | `[slot, state, kind, name…]` — slot 0–53, state = enum below, kind = agent-kind code below in the low 3 bits (v2: bit 6, `0x40`, set = the host is auto-approving this agent; v4: bit 5, `0x20`, set = repeat mode; v5: bit 4, `0x10`, set = in the marked group; v6: bit 3, `0x08`, set = the host holds prompts queued for it), then the agent's display name as ASCII (≤ 12 chars used on screen; ≤ 44 sent). State EMPTY with no name vacates the slot |
108	| 0x02 | DETAIL | `[line, text…]` — detail line for the *currently selected* agent (≤ 29 chars). The host sends a window of 6 lines (0–5) to a v2 device and scrolls it itself; 8 lines (0–7) to a v1 device, which scrolls locally. An empty text clears the line |
109	| 0x03 | META | `[agent_count, blocked_count, view?]` — header counts; v6: an optional third byte says what the host is showing on DETAIL (0 output, 1 INFO, 2 DIFF), drawn as a tag on that page |
110	| 0x04 | FOOTER | `[style, text…]` — the bottom line of every page (≤ 29 chars): the armed prompt preset, or a transient message (the result of an action, an agent that needs you). Style: 0 idle (grey), 1 info, 2 good, 3 warning, 4 error. The host times messages out by sending the next footer. *v2* |
111	| 0x05 | BEEP | `[sound, gain?]` — play a sound: 1 attention, 2 done, 3 error, 4 ack (a click) *(v2)*; 5 heads-up, 6 tick, 7 up, 8 down, 9 alert (an agent became BLOCKED) *(v5)*. v5: an optional second byte is the loudness in 64ths (64 or absent = as written, 127 ≈ twice that). An older device ignores the gain and plays nothing for a sound it does not know, so the host sends it only 1–4 |
112	| 0x06 | SELECT | `[slot]` — move the device's selection (and key page) to this slot; not echoed as CC 120. *v2* |
113	| 0x07 | TEXT | `[line, style, text…]` — the MENU page: line 0 is its title, 1–7 its rows (≤ 29 chars); v6: lines 8 and 9 are the host's two lines on the ABOUT page (its version and backend, its system; ≤ 19 chars). Style: the footer's 0–4, 5 cursor (bright), 6 plain text. *v3* |
114	| 0x08 | PAGE | `[page]` — turn the device to this page (0 GRID, 1 DETAIL, 2 APPROVALS, 3 MENU, 4 ABOUT *(v6)*); not echoed as CC 121. *v3* |
115	| 0x09 | KEYLEDS | `[mode × up to 27]` — the host's lights for keys 0–26, shown only while a button is held: 0 off, 1 glow, 2 on, 3 blink. An empty frame gives the keys back. *v3* |
116	| 0x0A | BTNLEDS | `[mode × up to 14]` — the host's lights for buttons 0–13 (the `BTN_*` ids): 0 the device decides, 1 off, 2 on, 3 blink, 4 glow. The host lights SEQ while the selected agent is on repeat and blinks SAVE when its prompt offers "don't ask again". *v4* |
117	| 0x0B | GAUGE | `[slot, percent]` — how full that agent's context is, 0–100; 127 = unknown (no gauge). Drawn as a bar at the end of the slot's row and under DETAIL's status line. Cleared by an EMPTY SLOT frame. *v5* |
118	| 0x0F | HELLO_ACK | `[proto_version]` — host is alive; the device shows `HOST OK` (v2: and answers with CC 120; v3: and CC 121) |
119	
120	Per refresh cycle (1 s, sooner after an action or a Herdr event) the host
121	sends: a META frame if the counts changed; a SLOT frame per slot whose
122	(state, kind, name, flags) changed, including an EMPTY one for a slot whose
123	agent went away; the selected agent's changed DETAIL lines; the FOOTER if it
124	changed. Every 10 s everything is re-sent unconditionally (a lost frame
125	heals itself). A device RESET (CC 118 = 0x7F) is sent only when a device
126	says hello or the daemon starts — not periodically, so the device's per-slot
127	clocks survive. A v2 device shows `NO HOST` again after 25 s without a frame.
128	
129	A v1 device ignores frame types it does not know, so the host sends
130	FOOTER/BEEP/SELECT/TEXT/PAGE/KEYLEDS/BTNLEDS regardless; it withholds only the SLOT flags an older
131	device would misread as part of the kind (auto before v2, repeat before v4, mark before v5, queue before v6),
132	GAUGE frames and the v5 sounds, and host-side scrolling.
133	
134	### State enum
135	
136	| Value | State | Meaning |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| 0 | EMPTY | No agent in this slot |
139	| 1 | IDLE | Agent is up, waiting for input |
140	| 2 | WORKING | Agent is producing output / running tools |
141	| 3 | BLOCKED | Agent is waiting on the human (permission prompt, question) |
142	| 4 | DONE | Agent finished its turn/task |
143	| 5 | ERROR | Agent process errored / exited badly |
144	| 6 | UNKNOWN | Backend can't tell |
145	
146	### Agent-kind codes
147	
148	0 unknown · 1 claude (Claude Code) · 2 codex · 3 opencode · 4 grok ·
149	5 copilot · 6 shell/other. Herdr's native agent names map onto these;
150	anything unrecognised maps to 6 (or 0 before detection).
151	
152	### LED rendering (device, per slot key)
153	
154	| State | Key LED |
155	|---|---|
156	| EMPTY | off |
157	| IDLE | dim glow (`fm1_led_key_glow`) |
158	| WORKING | solid on |
159	| BLOCKED | blink, 2 Hz (250 ms on / 250 ms off) |
160	| DONE | solid for 2 s after the transition, then dim glow |
161	| ERROR | fast blink, ~6 Hz |
162	| UNKNOWN | glow pulsing at 1 Hz (glow/off alternate each 500 ms) |
163	
164	The *selected* slot's LED is additionally forced on during the alternate
165	500 ms phase (except EMPTY, which only glows at 1 Hz) so you can always see
166	where you are. Button LEDs: PLAY lit while the selected agent is WORKING,
167	REC blinks while the selected agent is BLOCKED, ARP lit while the selected
168	agent is auto-approved, HOME/EDIT/GLO lit on their page.
169	
170	### Screen rendering (device)
171	
172	- Header: `AGENT DECK`, agent count, blocked count, `HOST OK` while frames
173	  keep arriving.
174	- **GRID page**: list of the current slot page (8 rows visible, follows the
175	  selection): slot number, state glyph (`-` EMPTY, `.` IDLE, `>` WORKING,
176	  `!` BLOCKED, `*` DONE, `x` ERROR, `?` UNKNOWN), name, how long the agent
177	  has been in that state (`7s`, `42m`, `13h` — counted on the device from
178	  the SLOT frame that changed it), `A` if auto-approved and `R` if on
179	  repeat. Selected row
180	  is prefixed with `>` cursor and drawn bright.
181	- **DETAIL page**: selected agent's name, state, kind and time in state,
182	  then 6 detail lines (K1 scrolls, via the host).
183	- **APPROVALS page**: the GRID filtered to BLOCKED slots only.
184	- **MENU page** (v3): eight lines of TEXT from the host — a title and seven
185	  rows. The device knows nothing about what they mean.
186	- **Footer** (every page): the host's FOOTER text; a per-page hint until
187	  the host has sent one.
188	
189	### Sound (device)
190	
191	The synth engine is gone, but the DAC is not: BEEP frames play short
192	triangle-wave sounds through the FM-1's own output, at the MASTER volume:
193	two rising calls for attention, C-E-G for done, two low notes for an
194	error, a click for ack; v5 adds a double note (heads-up), a tick, a rising
195	and a falling blip (feedback for the user's own actions) and the alert —
196	three rising calls, three times — for an agent that has become BLOCKED.
197	In v5 the host also sets each sound's loudness (BEEP's second byte): the
198	feedback sounds play at about a third of full, the alert near twice. The host decides when (state transitions it observes;
199	never on first sight of an agent), so a daemon restart does not set off
200	every chime at once.
201	
202	## Versioning
203	
204	`PROTO_VERSION = 6` in both the firmware (`firmware/agtdeck.c`) and the
205	daemon (`host/agtdeck.py`). The device announces its version in the boot
206	hello (CC 117) and in every heartbeat (CC 116); the host echoes its own in
207	HELLO_ACK. Either side can be the older one:
208	
209	- **v6 daemon, v5 device (firmware 0.5):** everything but the `Q` marker,
210	  the INFO / DIFF tag on DETAIL and the ABOUT page (MENU → ABOUT shows a
211	  text version instead). The colour screens are firmware 0.6's own.
212	- **v6 daemon, v4 device (firmware 0.4):** as above, and without the `+` marker,
213	  the context gauges, the feedback sounds and the loud alert (a BLOCKED
214	  agent gets the attention chime three times instead).
215	- **v6 daemon, v3 device (firmware 0.3):** as above, and without the `R`
216	  marker and the host's button lights (SEQ and LFO lit, SAVE blinking).
217	- **v6 daemon, v2 device (firmware 0.2):** everything but the chords and
218	  the MENU page; REC/FX/ENV/SEQ/SEL act on press, as before.
219	- **v6 daemon, v1 device (firmware 0.1):** every control still works —
220	  the device has always forwarded all of them. Missing are the things only
221	  new firmware can render: the footer line, the chimes, K4's jump (the
222	  device's cursor cannot be moved by the host), deep scrolling (K1 scrolls
223	  the 8 lines locally), the auto-approve marker and ARP LED.
224	- **v1 daemon, v2 device:** works as v1 did; that daemon's 10 s RESET
225	  restarts the per-slot clocks each time.
226	
227	New frame types must use unused type nibbles; new states/kinds append at
228	the end.
229	
230	## Flash-chip note (why this protocol doc mentions hardware)
231	
232	Kevin's unit is a late-2026 FM-1 with the **UC25HQ80** flash (JEDEC
233	`0xB36014`), not the early Puya P25Q80 (`0x856014`). The on-device gate is
234	`FL_JEDEC_OK(id)` in `vendor-dinghy/firmware/hal/fm1_flash_map.h`, used by
235	`platform.c`, `recovery.c` and the update loader (`loader.c`). **Dinghy 0.5
236	already accepts both IDs for the FM-1** —
237	`((id) == 0x856014u || (id) == 0xB36014u)` — so no allowlist change is needed;
238	if a future platform drops it, that one line is the fix. The host-side
239	installer `tools/fm1_install.py` performs no flash-ID check at all (it just
240	speaks the OTA SysEx protocol). See README.md for the arrival-day sequence.
241
```

````text
<p align="center"><img src="assets/logo.svg" width="96" alt="Dinghy"></p>

# Dinghy

**The smallest firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 to build your own on.**

Dinghy plays a sine wave on the keys, and that is all it does. Under it is everything an FM-1 firmware needs
before it can be any fun: the update path, the USB rescue, MIDI over USB and the TRS jack (with clock), USB audio, the
keys, knobs and LEDs, the screen, flash storage, and the same again for the M-Vave SMK-37. It all works, so you start
with the part you actually want to write.

```
firmware/src/dinghy.c     <- your firmware: ~300 lines, a 4-voice sine. Start here.
firmware/src/platform.c   <- the plumbing (boot, USB, MIDI, updates, audio ISR, storage). Done; read it, don't fight it.
firmware/src/store.h      <- where your data lives in flash, per board
firmware/src/*.c, hal/    <- Felucca's platform, as SLOOP / sloopDX / OberVave carry it; the SMK-37 layer
```

Dinghy is based on [Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca) by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments), with its
platform as [SLOOP](https://github.com/isod89/sloop-fm1) (isod89) carries it: it keeps that platform and throws away the
rest. The smallest boat of the family, after the felucca and the sloop.

<p align="center"><img src="docs/screen.png" width="240" alt="Dinghy's screen: the name, the note played, a keyboard with the keys that sound"></p>

> **Status: 0.5.** 0.5 runs on newer FM-1s too: their flash chip, the UC25HQ80 (0xB36014), beside the Puya (0x856014);
> before, a firmware built on Dinghy saved to RAM only on them. Dinghy's platform runs on the FM-1 in VIBE FM Link
> (zvenson/vibe-link), tested there on 7.11.2026. 0.3 was tested on the FM-1: the install, MIDI in (pitch exact, 4 voices), USB audio at
> 44.1 / 48 kHz, the keys, the screen, the octave kept in flash, and back to another firmware through the hub.
> 0.4 brings OberVave's platform over: the TRS MIDI IN, the clock, blobs and slots, the loader's screen, the SMK-37.
> That code runs on the device in OberVave (FM-1 and SMK-37); Dinghy 0.4 itself is tested on the host only so far.

## What you get

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Updates that always work** | `tools/fm1_install.py`, the web installers and the [FM-1 Firmware Hub](https://thefirmwarehub.com) reach your firmware over USB, so you (and your users) can always install the next build, or go back to the official firmware. |
| **USB rescue** | Hold **OCT-** while switching on: no sound, only the updater. If your firmware crashes twice at boot, the FM-1 goes there by itself. |
| **MIDI** | USB in and out (class compliant) and the FM-1's TRS MIDI IN, in one queue: `midi_get()` says where a message came from, `midi_send()`. Clock, start, stop and continue reach your app. |
| **USB audio** | The FM-1 shows up as a 16-bit stereo audio input (44.1 or 48 kHz): record it into any DAW or phone. Nothing to do. |
| **Panel** | 27 keys, 14 buttons, 7 encoders, the MASTER knob, the LEDs, by name (`BTN_PLAY`, `ENC_KNOB1`, ...). |
| **Screen** | 240 x 240, text in two sizes, rectangles, lines, pixels. |
| **Storage** | `settings_*` (4 KB), 8 blobs of 4 KB (`blob_*`), 8 slots of 16 KB (`slot_*`), each with a CRC, in places no other part of the flash is in reach of. |
| **Never waits for the screen** | `LCD_IDLE`: your app reads MIDI and the keys while the screen's DMA runs, so a chord never stumbles over a redraw. |
| **The SMK-37 too** | `./build.sh --board smk37` (Pro, Elite, MKE-P37): the same app on M-Vave's 37-key keyboard, with velocity, outer keys, 16 coloured pads, faders and wheels. [docs/SMK37.md](docs/SMK37.md) |
| **An update screen** | The update loader draws your name in your colour, a progress bar and what to do, also after an install was cut off (FM-1). |
| **A crash screen** | A fault shows where it happened (the PC), then the FM-1 restarts. |
| **Host mode** | The same `dinghy.c` on your computer: the screen as an image, the sound as a WAV, scripted keys, knobs, MIDI (USB and TRS, a clock), SMK-37 pads and wheels. No FM-1 needed to try an idea. |
| **Tests and CI** | `tests/run_tests.sh`: the host app, the flash maps, the update path, the loader, the installer. A tag `vX.Y` on GitHub builds, tests and releases the packages with a build attestation. |
| **Checks** | The build fails on what bricks or breaks an FM-1 firmware: a 64-bit division, a call into the chip ROM, too much RAM, a register touched outside `hal/`. |

## Build your own

From nothing to your own firmware on the FM-1, step by step. Each step works before you go to the next.

### 1. Copy it

On GitHub: **Use this template** (top right on this page) or fork it, then clone your copy. Rename nothing yet:
first make sure the unchanged Dinghy builds on your machine.

### 2. Set up once

You need Linux on x86-64 (or macOS / Windows with Docker or WSL), Python 3 with Pillow, the JieLi toolchain
and three files of the JieLi AC79 SDK:

```sh
pip3 install Pillow mido python-rtmidi
tools/get_toolchain.sh                      # JieLi's clang for the chip, to ~/.jieli/toolchain
git clone --depth 1 --branch AC79NN_SDK_V1.2.1_2023-12-13 \
    https://gitee.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK.git ~/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK
```

On macOS the build runs the toolchain in a `linux/amd64` Docker container by itself (have Docker running).
`JIELI_TOOLCHAIN` and `AC79_SDK` point elsewhere if your copies live somewhere else.

### 3. Hear it without an FM-1

```sh

# Build Dinghy (see README.md).

#   AC79_SDK         JieLi AC79 SDK checkout (default: ~/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK)

export JIELI_TOOLCHAIN="${JIELI_TOOLCHAIN:-$HOME/.jieli/toolchain}"
export AC79_SDK="${AC79_SDK:-$HOME/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK}"
PY="${PYTHON:-python3}"

"$PY" -c 'import PIL' 2>/dev/null || { echo "build.sh: $PY has no Pillow (pip3 install Pillow)"; exit 1; }
[ -x "$JIELI_TOOLCHAIN/pi32v2/bin/clang" ] || { echo "build.sh: no toolchain in $JIELI_TOOLCHAIN (run tools/get_toolchain.sh)"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$AC79_SDK/cpu/wl82/tools/uboot.boot" ] || { echo "build.sh: no JieLi AC79 SDK in $AC79_SDK"; exit 1; }
if [ "$(uname -s)" != Linux ] || [ "$(uname -m)" != x86_64 ]; then
    docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "build.sh: Docker is not running"; exit 1; }
fi
exec "$PY" tools/build.py "$@"
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only */
/* Agent Deck: the FM-1 as a control surface for CLI coding agents.
 *
 * A Dinghy app (platform.c below is Felucca/SLOOP's, via Dinghy — see
 * LICENSING.md in the Dinghy tree). The synth engine is gone; the only
 * sound left is a handful of alert chimes the host asks for. The panel
 * talks to a host daemon (host/agtdeck.py) over USB-MIDI channel 16; the
 * wire format is PROTOCOL.md in this project (this is protocol v6). In short:
 *
 *   out: keys = Note On/Off 48..74 (a press also selects the slot),
 *        buttons = CC 102..115, encoders = CC 85..91 (relative),
 *        MASTER = CC 7, CC 116 = 1 s heartbeat (value = protocol version),
 *        CC 117 = hello (protocol version), CC 120 = the selected slot
 *        and CC 121 = the page, when they change here or when the host
 *        says hello.
 *   in:  a framed byte stream, CC 118 = frame control (0x10|type start,
 *        0x20 end, 0x7F reset), CC 119 = one payload byte. SysEx never
 *        reaches an app in this platform (the updater owns it), hence CCs.
 *        Frames: SLOT, DETAIL, META, FOOTER, BEEP, SELECT, TEXT, PAGE,
 *        KEYLEDS, BTNLEDS, GAUGE, HELLO_ACK.
 *
 * The device is deliberately dumb: the host owns everything that needs
 * judgement (what a knob does to an agent, which prompt is armed, when to
 * chime, how far the detail text is scrolled) and the device renders it.
 * What stays local is what must feel instant: the selection cursor, the
 * page (ALGORITHM turns, GLO/HOME/EDIT jump), the LEDs, the clocks.
 *
 * Pages: GRID (the slot list, with how long each agent has been in its
 * state), DETAIL (the selected agent's output, as the host windows it),
 * APPROVALS (the BLOCKED slots), MENU (eight lines of text the host
 * writes: its menus; SELECT is the host's there), ABOUT (this app, this
 * device, the host: drawn here). OCT-/OCT+ page the 54
 * slots, 27 keys at a time. A key pressed while a button is held is a
 * chord: it goes to the host without moving the cursor, and while the
 * button is held the host may light the keys its own way (KEYLEDS). The bottom line of every page is the host's footer (the armed
 * prompt, the result of the last action). Settings kept in flash: the
 * selected slot and the page.
 *
 * Rules of the road (the chip has no FPU and no libgcc): integers only,
 * no float, no 64-bit division. tests/host.c runs this file on a computer.
 */
#define APP_NAME "AGTDECK"
#define CV_MAX (240u * 192u)                    /* one big canvas: the list area */
static void app_idle(void);
#define LCD_IDLE app_idle                       /* while the screen's DMA runs: MIDI in (platform.c) */
#include "platform.c"

/* ---- the sound: alert chimes only. The host asks for one with a BEEP
 * frame; the main loop hands it to the audio interrupt through beep_seq /
 * beep_id (one writer: the main loop). MASTER is the volume (platform.c).
 * A tone is a triangle with a linear decay; {phase step, frames, decay}:
 * step = f * 2^32 / 44100, decay = (BEEP_AMP << 8) / frames, both worked
 * out here so the interrupt never divides. step 0 is a rest. */
#define BEEP_AMP 12000
typedef struct { uint32_t inc; uint16_t n; uint16_t dec; } tone_t;
static const tone_t PAT_ATTENTION[] = {         /* an agent needs you: two rising calls */
    {85704563u, 3969, 773}, {114435070u, 3969, 773}, {0, 2646, 0},
    {85704563u, 3969, 773}, {114435070u, 6174, 497}, {0, 0, 0}};
static const tone_t PAT_DONE[] = {              /* an agent finished: C E G */
    {50960128u, 3528, 870}, {64205378u, 3528, 870}, {76354000u, 7056, 435}, {0, 0, 0}};
static const tone_t PAT_ERROR[] = {             /* something broke: two low notes */
    {19088744u, 7056, 435}, {0, 2646, 0}, {19088744u, 11466, 267}, {0, 0, 0}};
static const tone_t PAT_ACK[] = {{152709948u, 1544, 1989}, {0, 0, 0}};   /* a click: done as told */
static const tone_t PAT_WARN[] = {              /* heads up, no hurry: one note, twice */
    {64278423u, 2646, 1161}, {0, 1764, 0}, {64278423u, 2646, 1161}, {0, 0, 0}};
static const tone_t PAT_TICK[] = {{194783100u, 441, 6965}, {0, 0, 0}};   /* feedback: a control moved */
static const tone_t PAT_UP[] = {                /* feedback: sent / approved */
    {85704563u, 1764, 1741}, {114435070u, 1764, 1741}, {0, 0, 0}};
static const tone_t PAT_DOWN[] = {              /* feedback: denied / stopped */
    {114435070u, 1764, 1741}, {85704563u, 1764, 1741}, {0, 0, 0}};
static const tone_t PAT_ALERT[] = {             /* an agent is BLOCKED: three rising calls, thrice */
    {85704563u, 3528, 870}, {114435070u, 3528, 870}, {152709948u, 3528, 870}, {0, 3528, 0},
    {85704563u, 3528, 870}, {114435070u, 3528, 870}, {152709948u, 3528, 870}, {0, 3528, 0},
    {85704563u, 3528, 870}, {114435070u, 3528, 870}, {152709948u, 10584, 290}, {0, 0, 0}};
#define NPATTERNS 9u
static const tone_t *const PATTERNS[NPATTERNS] = {PAT_ATTENTION, PAT_DONE, PAT_ERROR, PAT_ACK, PAT_WARN,
                                                  PAT_TICK, PAT_UP, PAT_DOWN, PAT_ALERT};
static volatile uint32_t beep_seq;
static volatile uint8_t beep_id, beep_gain = 64;   /* gain in 64ths: 64 is as written, 127 twice that */

I can't reproduce the full README verbatim here, since quotes are limited to 125 characters. Below is a condensed summary of the page's content.

**Overview**
- **Name:** codex-midi (scf4/codex-midi), public, MIT-licensed, 9 stars, 2 forks, 11 commits on `main`.
- **Purpose:** Emulates a Codex Micro so ChatGPT Codex can be controlled with other input devices, such as MIDI controllers, Stream Decks, and game controllers. "Control Codex on macOS with almost any input device."
- **Status:** Independent project, not affiliated with OpenAI, Work Louder, PreSonus, or other manufacturers.

**Platform and runtime**
- macOS only, with the ChatGPT desktop app installed.
- Bun 1.3.14 or newer. The project includes a `tsconfig.json`, so it is TypeScript.
- Optional: `node` on `PATH`, needed only for the preload compatibility test.
- The tested ChatGPT app version is not stated.

**Architecture (three replaceable boundaries)**
1. **Controller surface:** converts hardware input into normalized Micro events and allowlisted controller actions. MIDI is one implementation.
2. **Project2077 engine:** implements the Codex Micro HID/RPC report model.
3. **ChatGPT host transport:** exposes the synthetic device and forwards controller actions to the launched ChatGPT process over a private Unix socket.

**Preload shim and node-hid**
- The preload intercepts only the Work Louder device kit's matching `node-hid` request and passes unrelated HID calls through unchanged.
- A physical Codex Micro takes precedence over the synthetic descriptor.
- JSON-RPC methods are not listed on the page.

**Adapters**
- **PreSonus ATOM (`"type": "atom"`):** the bundled reference adapter, implemented with verified Codex Micro controls and RGB feedback.
- **Other devices:** created with the `add-controller` skill. A controller counts as supported only after a documented physical-device test passes. Until then, it is "implemented but unverified."

**Actions**
- Controller actions use a fixed allowlist. Adapters cannot request arbitrary code or keyboard input.
- ATOM actions include showing or hiding sidebars, toggling Plan mode, expanding panels, task navigation, scrolling, Submit, Fast, Approve, Reject, Fork, and opening Codex Micro settings.

**Task slots and states**
- Six task pads select task slots.
- Slot states: idle, thinking, complete, needs-input, error.

**Configuration and setup**
- Config file: `codex-midi.json` in the project root, created by guided setup. Comments and trailing commas are accepted.
- Use `bun run midi:list` to find port names (`inputName`, and `outputName` if needed).
- Manual launch: `bun install`, then `bun run launch`. The launcher does not modify ChatGPT, install a service, or create a login item.
- Verification: `bun run verify` type-checks and runs the Bun test suite.

**Security**
- No network listener. Reports stay on a private Unix socket.
- Manual launch uses a per-launch token scoped to the launched ChatGPT process.
- The page says this is a compatibility shim around a private app integration, not a security boundary, and advises reviewing the source before running it.

**Repository root files and directories**

- `package.json`
- `tsconfig.json`

**Caveat:** The page doesn't cover several items you asked about, including the HID descriptor, the task-slot states, and the exact preload load mechanism. I've noted those gaps below rather than filling them in.

**HID and report format**
- Reports are 64 bytes. Project2077 uses report ID `6` and channel `2` for JSON-RPC.
- Each report has a payload-length byte and up to 61 bytes of UTF-8 payload.
- The engine reassembles multi-report requests and frames responses. It emits `v.oai.hid` key events and `v.oai.rad` joystick events.
- The HID descriptor itself is not described.

**JSON-RPC methods**

| Method | Result or effect |
|---|---|
| `sys.version` | Emulated firmware version (`0.3.0`) |
| `device.status` | Emulated battery (`100`) and charging (`true`) |
| `v.oai.thstatus` | Six task-feedback records |
| `v.oai.rgbcfg` | Key and ambient feedback configuration |

Unknown methods are explicitly rejected. The page describes the `v.oai.hid` and `v.oai.rad` names as event outputs, not RPC methods.

**Preload shim and ChatGPT modification**
- Manual launch loads a dependency-free CommonJS preload into one ChatGPT process tree.
- It intercepts only the Work Louder device kit's `node-hid` load. It adds one synthetic Project2077 descriptor and passes real devices and other `node-hid` calls through unchanged.
- It does not modify or re-sign `ChatGPT.app`.
- The page doesn't name an environment variable or say exactly how the preload is injected.

**Updates**
- The private action translation targets ChatGPT 26.715.31925 (build 5551).
- It is isolated because it is an app-compatibility surface and may need adjustment after a ChatGPT update.

**Adapter interface**
- A `ControllerDefinition` supplies a display name and builds a controller surface from a context with logging and controller-action dispatch.
- The surface starts with the normalized Micro input sink, may consume Codex feedback (optional), and stops cleanly.
- MIDI devices usually declare a `MidiControllerProfile` and use `createMidiSurface()`.
- Definitions are listed explicitly in `src/controllers/index.ts`, with no scanning or plugins.

**Actions**
- `CodexAppAction` is a finite union covering sidebar controls, task navigation, task scrolling, Plan mode, the default environment action, and Codex Micro settings.
- Controllers cannot supply arbitrary commands, routes, scripts, selectors, shell commands, or shortcuts.
- Requests time out after two seconds, are never retried, and fail nonfatally.
- Scrolling uses precise wheel events, and its step size follows the input rate.

**Task slots and states**
- `v.oai.thstatus` returns six task-feedback records.
- The page doesn't define the individual slots or the states they can hold.

/* ---- the screen. Two canvases, drawn one after the other into the same
 * buffer: the header (240 x 56, top of the LCD) and the page (240 x 184
 * below it). Colour means state everywhere: amber is waiting on you, green
 * is finished, red is broken, white is working, grey is at rest. */
#define C_ACC RGB(120, 200, 255)
#define C_TXT RGB(200, 200, 200)
#define C_GREY RGB(112, 112, 112)
#define C_FAINT RGB(64, 64, 64)
#define C_RULE RGB(50, 50, 50)
#define C_WARN RGB(255, 180, 60)
#define C_BAD RGB(255, 90, 70)
#define C_GOOD RGB(120, 255, 146)
#define C_VIOLET RGB(190, 150, 255)
#define C_SELBG RGB(20, 44, 78)                 /* behind the selected row */
#define C_BODY RGB(26, 30, 40)                  /* the logo's body */

static uint16_t dim4(uint16_t c) { return (uint16_t)((c >> 2) & 0x39E7u); }   /* a quarter as bright: fills behind text */
static uint16_t dim2(uint16_t c) { return (uint16_t)((c >> 1) & 0x7BEFu); }

static uint16_t state_colour(uint8_t s)
{
    return s == S_BLOCKED ? C_WARN : s == S_ERROR ? C_BAD :
           s == S_DONE ? C_GOOD : s == S_WORKING ? C_WHITE : C_GREY;
}
static const char *const KIND_TAG[7] = {"??", "CL", "CX", "OC", "GK", "CP", "SH"};
static uint16_t kind_colour(uint8_t k)
{
    return k == 1u ? RGB(235, 145, 95) : k == 2u ? RGB(90, 205, 175) : k == 3u ? C_VIOLET :
           k == 4u ? RGB(225, 225, 225) : k == 5u ? RGB(120, 170, 255) : C_GREY;
}
static uint16_t gauge_colour(uint32_t pct)
{
    return pct >= 85u ? C_BAD : pct >= 60u ? C_WARN : C_ACC;
}

static void rrect(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t w, int32_t h, uint16_t c)   /* a filled box with its corners off */
{
    cv_rect(x + 2, y, w - 4, h, c);
    cv_rect(x + 1, y + 1, w - 2, h - 2, c);
    cv_rect(x, y + 2, w, h - 4, c);
}

/* ---- LEDs */
static uint8_t led_mode(uint32_t slot, uint32_t now)
{
    uint8_t st = slot_state[slot];
    uint32_t phase500 = (now / 500u) & 1u;
    if (st == S_EMPTY) return slot == sel_slot ? (phase500 ? 1u : 0u) : 0u;
    if (st == S_IDLE) return slot == sel_slot && phase500 ? 2u : 1u;
    if (st == S_WORKING) return 2u;
    if (st == S_BLOCKED) return ((now / 250u) & 1u) ? 2u : 0u;
    if (st == S_DONE) return now - slot_since[slot] < 2000u ? 2u : 1u;
    if (st == S_ERROR) return ((now / 167u) & 1u) ? 2u : 0u;
    return phase500 ? 1u : 0u;                  /* UNKNOWN: glow pulsing at 1 Hz */
}

Host mode runs the same `dinghy.c` on your computer: the sound as a WAV, the screen as images. Most ideas can be
tried here first, in seconds.

### 4. Your first change

Open [firmware/src/dinghy.c](firmware/src/dinghy.c) (~200 lines). The sound is `app_audio()`: it gets an empty
buffer of stereo frames and adds to it. Make the sine a square:

```c
s = ((int32_t)ph < 0 ? 8000 : -8000) * amp >> 15;     /* instead of s = (sine(ph) * amp) >> 15; */
```

Run `tests/run_host.sh` again and listen to `build/host/dinghy.wav`. The screen is drawn in `app_main()`, the keys
are read there too: change the text, add a knob ([docs/API.md](docs/API.md) has every call).

### 5. Onto the FM-1

```sh
./build.sh                                       # -> build/dinghy.fwsc (fails on what would brick the FM-1)
python3 tools/fm1_install.py build/dinghy.fwsc   # over USB; asks before it writes, restarts into your build
python3 tools/fm1_install.py --info              # what runs on the connected FM-1
```

That is the whole loop: change, hear it on the host, build, install. Back to another firmware, or to the official
one, with the [FM-1 Firmware Hub](https://thefirmwarehub.com) in Chrome or Edge: Dinghy (and every copy of it)
answers the hub's updater like every firmware there. Installing firmware is at your own risk.

### 6. When it goes wrong

- **It crashes:** the screen shows where (the PC), then the FM-1 restarts. Twice at boot and it goes to the
  USB rescue by itself.
- **It won't start at all:** hold **OCT-** while switching on: the USB rescue, no sound, only the updater. Install
  a working build (or another firmware from the hub) from there.
- **The build refuses:** it checks for a 64-bit division, a call into the chip ROM, too much RAM, a register touched
  outside `hal/`. [docs/RULES.md](docs/RULES.md) says why each one matters; read it before your first crash.

### 7. Make it yours, release it, get into the hub

Your name and logo, your own package identity (so the FM-1 and the installers tell your firmware from Dinghy),
a GitHub release with the `.fwsc`, and how to get listed next to the others in the
[FM-1 Firmware Hub](https://thefirmwarehub.com): **[docs/MAKE-IT-YOURS.md](docs/MAKE-IT-YOURS.md)**.

## Where to go next

- **[docs/API.md](docs/API.md)**: everything `platform.c` gives you, with the panel's ids, the screen calls, the
  audio contract, MIDI, storage, the flash map, timing, the SMK-37.
- **[docs/SMK37.md](docs/SMK37.md)**: building and installing for the M-Vave SMK-37.
- **[docs/MAKE-IT-YOURS.md](docs/MAKE-IT-YOURS.md)**: turn Dinghy into your firmware: the name, the package
  identity, releases, getting into the FM-1 Firmware Hub.
- **[docs/RULES.md](docs/RULES.md)**: the chip's rules (no FPU, no libgcc, the audio ISR's budget) and what the build
  checks for you. Read it before your first crash, not after.

## License

GPL-3.0-only, as Felucca and SLOOP: you may change and share it, and whoever gets your firmware gets its source.
Details, credits and third-party parts in [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).

The platform is Copyright (C) 2026 Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments, with SLOOP's changes (isod89);
the SMK-37 layer by M. Geisler (genkigenki); the loader's screen after Skiff (illuminus5). Dinghy (the app, the host
mode, the docs) by zvenson.

19	
20	`just emu-run` 單獨開只會停在 `NO HOST`，因為沒有 daemon。開兩個 terminal：
21	
22	```sh
23	# terminal 1：模擬器，插上虛擬 USB 線（等同 emu-run … --usb）
24	just agtdeck-emu
25	
26	# terminal 2：daemon 的硬體模式（不是 --simulate），會找到名為 "FM-1 AGTDECK (emu)" 的 MIDI 裝置

29	
30	2026-11-17 實測成功 `[模擬]`：模擬器畫面從 `NO HOST` 變成 `HOST`，列出 Herdr 的 pane（名稱、種類 `SH` / `CL`、停留時間），標頭顯示 blocked 數與總數。daemon 端印出 `[midi] in='FM-1 AGTDECK (emu)'` 與 `[device] firmware speaks proto v6`。

Advanced commands:

 `https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core`

```text
# herdr-core (`hc`) Summary

**What it is:** `hc` runs programs and coding agents in terminals that keep running after you disconnect. Agents can start other agents, send them work, and receive their replies. You can attach to any terminal and take over. The page says "Core draws nothing," so it has no interface of its own. You use it from a shell, an agent, or your own app. The repository is public, Apache-2.0 licensed, and has 762 stars, 191 forks, and 213 commits on `master`.

**Install and update**
- Linux and macOS (x86_64 and aarch64) use a shell install script. Windows (x86_64) uses a PowerShell script. Linux builds are static.
- On Windows, templates and quoted shell commands need `sh` on PATH, such as the one Git for Windows provides.
- `hc update` updates the binary. Running terminals keep running.
- `hc server restart` keeps the core's environment. `--fresh`, run from outside Herdr, picks up the calling shell's environment without ending programs.

**CLI commands**
- `hc run cargo test`: streams output and waits.
- `hc run --bg --name web bun dev`: starts a program and returns.
- `hc run --keep`: keeps a terminal alive if its program is lost. Recovery starts a fresh shell and never reruns the task.
- `hc ls`: lists live terminals. The page does not document `--json`.
- `hc attach web`: takes over a terminal. Ctrl+\ detaches.
- `hc read web --lines 100`: reads output without attaching.
- `hc send review "..."`: sends input to a terminal. Sends wait while a draft is unfinished.
- `hc wait --children all`: waits for child terminals.
- `hc get review`: takes a status snapshot.
- `hc events`: follows changes.
- `hc templates`: lists reusable agent roles.
- `hc schema`: prints the API as OpenRPC with JSON Schema.
- `hc connect`: carries the protocol over stdin and stdout, including over SSH.
- `hc --skill`: prints agent-facing docs.
- `hc --licenses`: prints third-party licenses.
- `hc --help` and `hc <command> --help`: built-in help.

**Core API**
- The API is described as OpenRPC with JSON Schema, generated by `hc schema`.
- `schema/README.md` covers connecting, terminal streams, events, and status.
- The page does not name the transport (Unix socket, WebSocket, or HTTP) or the authentication method. Those details are in the linked schema and security docs.
- The event stream format is not described on this page.

**Terminal and status model**
- Agents can report working, done, blocked, or error states.
- Core stores what a program reports. It does not infer status from screen text or identify agent brands. A program that reports nothing has no status.
- Parents receive notes when a child needs attention or ends.
- Children end with their parent unless started with `--outlive-parent`.
- On Unix, ending a terminal hangs up its program and foreground job. Programs detached with `nohup` or `setsid` can keep running.

**OSC 7501 Program Status Protocol**
- Programs report status through OSC 7501.
- The page does not give the byte sequences, the full state list, which agents emit it natively, or whether hooks exist.

**Configuration** (`~/.config/herdr-core/config.toml`; on Windows `%APPDATA%\herdr-core\config.toml`)
- `shell = ["nu"]`: sets the default shell as an executable followed by separate arguments. Without it, the default is `$SHELL` or `/bin/sh` on Unix, and PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell on Windows.
- `restore_screen = true`: shows a lost kept program's last saved screen above the new shell. Defaults to false.
- `notes_quiet = 3` and `draft_wait = 60`: control how long delivery waits for quiet and for unfinished drafts.

**Remote machines**
- `hc machine add my-ssh-host --name box` registers a machine.
- `hc run --on box --cwd /srv/app cargo test` runs a program remotely.
- Programs and files stay on the remote machine. The local core shows remote terminals in the same list.
- Supports SSH, custom connections, remote files, and reconnecting.

**Relationship to classic Herdr TUI:** Not covered on this page.

**Version and release date:** Not stated. The page mentions version 0.1.19 only as the target of an update path. The footer shows © 2026.

**Documentation links** (all under `github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/master/`)
- `docs/commands.md`: command reference, generated from the binary's help.
- `docs/machines.md`: cross-machine work.
- `docs/templates.md`: reusable agent roles.
- `docs/security.md`: access, state, updates, and signing.
- `schema/README.md`: API for building clients.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: contributor setup and checks.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `SECURITY.md`, and `AGENTS.md` are also in the repository.
- `https://herdr.dev/core`: project site.
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Agent Deck host daemon.

Bridges the M-VAVE FM-1 "Agent Deck" firmware (USB-MIDI channel 16, see
../PROTOCOL.md) to CLI coding agents running on this computer, via one of two
backends:

  * herdr  - the Herdr terminal multiplexer (herdr.dev). Preferred: it detects
             agents and reports Idle/Working/Blocked/Done natively over its
             newline-delimited JSON socket API.
  * tmux   - plain tmux panes; agent kind and state are heuristics over
             `pane_current_command` and captured pane content.

The device is a dumb panel; this daemon owns the behaviour. What the panel
does (the full table is in README.md):

  keys        select a slot                 SELECT    move the selection
  PLAY        start / continue; on an       K1        scroll the detail text
              empty slot: spawn an agent    K2        Up / Down in the agent
  REC         approve                       K3        Left / Right in the agent
  SAVE        approve, don't ask again      K4        jump to the next agent
  FX          deny (Esc)                              that needs you
  ENV         interrupt (Ctrl-C)            PRESETS   arm a prompt preset
  SEL         Enter                         SEQ       send the armed prompt
  LFO         cycle the agent's mode        ARP       toggle auto-approve
              (Shift+Tab)                   EDIT      detail page + focus the
  GLO (held)  + REC / FX / ENV / SEQ / ARP:           pane on the computer
              the same, for every agent it applies to

  Chords (firmware 0.3): hold a button, tap keys - the cursor stays put.
    REC / FX / ENV + key   approve / deny / interrupt that agent
    SEQ + key N            send prompt preset N to the selected agent
    SEL + key N            answer option N (types the digit 1-9)
    PLAY + key             start that agent / spawn one on an empty key
    SAVE + key             move the selected agent to that key
    SEQ held ~1 s          repeat the armed prompt at this agent each time
                           it finishes a turn (again to stop)
    EDIT on DETAIL         cycle the agent's OUTPUT, INFO (what it was
                           asked, what it wants, context size, git) and
                           DIFF (what it has changed in its repository)
    LFO + key              mark / unmark that agent; while any are marked,
                           GLO + button acts on the marked ones only
                           (GLO + LFO clears the marks)
    ARP + key              toggle auto-approve on that agent
    HOME on the GRID       the list, or the agents as coloured boxes
                           (firmware 0.6)
    GLO on APPROVALS       jump to the agent that has waited longest
  Knobs with a button held:
    PLAY + PRESETS         choose which agent PLAY starts
    SEQ + PRESETS          how many times repeat mode sends
    SEL + K1               scroll DETAIL a page at a time
    LFO + K4               step through the marked agents
  A prompt sent to a BLOCKED agent is queued and goes out once it is
  free; a preset may be a list of steps, sent one per finished turn.
  MENU page (ALGORITHM): SELECT moves (K1: a page at a time), SEL picks,
    FX backs out - this agent, fleet, new agent, send prompt, event log,
    close agent, settings, help, about.
  ABOUT page (firmware 0.6): the app, the device, this daemon.

Core uses only the Python 3 standard library. Real-MIDI mode additionally
needs `mido` (+ `python-rtmidi`), imported lazily, so `--simulate` runs
anywhere.

Usage:
  python3 agtdeck.py --backend auto|herdr|tmux [--simulate]
                       [--port SUBSTRING] [--herdr-session NAME]
                       [--herdr-socket PATH] [--poll SECONDS]
                       [--config PATH] [--no-wait]
  python3 agtdeck.py --doctor              check the setup and report
  python3 agtdeck.py --install-service     start at every login
  python3 agtdeck.py --uninstall-service

Without an FM-1 the daemon waits for one, and when the FM-1 is unplugged it
waits for it to come back and sends everything again.

Simulate mode reads commands from stdin, one per line:
  select N | start | approve | always | deny | interrupt | enter | mode
  auto | focus | next | prev | scroll N | preset N | send | prompt TEXT
  spawn [KIND] | all approve|deny|interrupt|send | keys K [K...]
  btn NAME [up|down] | enc NAME N | key N [up] | page N
  view | repeat | move N | copy | mark [N] | unmark | urgent | mute
  queue | quit
(`btn` / `enc` / `key` / `page` replay a panel control exactly as the FM-1
would send it; `btn NAME` alone is a tap, down then up.)
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import collections
import glob
import queue
import re
import shutil
